Before a team project starts, I accepted a role without comparing requirements to my skills or verifying coverage.
Reviewing the deck, I tested two opening slides with peers, gathered notes, and confirmed which version to keep.
Reviewing the deck, I chose an opening slide after a quick skim and did not test with peers or confirm the choice.
From the course list, I mapped electives to program pathways and verified the one that fits the required track.
From the course list, I added an elective by title and did not map it to pathways or verify track fit.
Though my peers rush, I listed opening points, compared them to new metrics, and confirmed which one to lead with.
Though my peers rush, I used the first opening point and did not compare it to metrics or confirm a lead.
Once I read the guide, I matched citation elements to the rules and verified the format line by line.
Once I read the guide, I chose a familiar format and did not match elements to rules or verify line by line.
While designing the lab plan, I listed risks, set thresholds, and checked steps against those thresholds.
While designing the lab plan, I fixed the step order and did not list risks, set thresholds, or check against them.
After my training list was set, I simulated load across orders, reviewed recovery, and confirmed a starting sequence.
After my training list was set, I ran drills in written order and did not simulate load, review recovery, or confirm a start.
At the whiteboard, I tested candidate examples, compared steps, and verified the one that isolates the core idea.
At the whiteboard, I kept the first example and did not test candidates, compare steps, or verify isolation of the idea.
After the seminar, I ranked readings by relevance and method notes and confirmed the paper to add.
After the seminar, I added a reading by title and did not rank by relevance or confirm method notes.
While updating my planner, I ranked duties by deadline and dependency and confirmed the first slot accordingly.
While updating my planner, I placed duties as recalled and did not rank by deadline or dependency or confirm the slot.
As I edit the paper, I compared graph types to the claim and verified the option that represents the relation clearly.
As I edit the paper, I inserted a graph without comparing it to the claim or verifying how it represents the relation.
In my weekly budget, I reviewed deferral options, compared effects, and confirmed which expense to delay.
In my weekly budget, I cut or kept items without reviewing deferrals, comparing effects, or confirming which to delay.
When drafting conclusions, I aligned arguments with the thesis checks and verified the one that meets the checks.
When drafting conclusions, I inserted an argument without aligning it to thesis checks or verifying that it meets them.
At the practice field, I compared drill orders with recovery windows and confirmed a rotation against those windows.
At the practice field, I ran drills back-to-back and did not compare orders with recovery windows or confirm a rotation.
On entering the study hall, I weighed tasks for tomorrow’s quiz and confirmed the topic to begin with.
On entering the study hall, I started the first task I saw and did not weigh tasks or confirm the starting topic.
Though the deadline is close, I tested slide variants, compared coverage of the claim, and verified one to use.
Though the deadline is close, I kept my first slide and did not test variants, compare coverage, or verify choice.
While sorting readings, I filtered by design and sample size and confirmed the paper that fits the question.
While sorting readings, I grabbed a nearby paper and did not filter by design or size or confirm fit to the question.
When picking club events, I checked schedule clashes, reviewed lab times, and confirmed the set to keep.
When picking club events, I signed up in sequence and did not check clashes, review lab times, or confirm the set.
At the kitchen table, I compared recipes by ingredients and prep time and verified one within the set window.
At the kitchen table, I chose a recipe by picture and did not compare ingredients or time or verify the window.
After scanning the files, I ranked datasets by error rate and confirmed which one to clean first.
After scanning the files, I opened a dataset at random and did not rank error rates or confirm which to clean first.
With draft points listed, I tested themes against scope and audience and verified the theme to adopt.
With draft points listed, I attached a theme without testing it against scope or audience or verifying adoption.
While preparing the poster, I compared color palettes to contrast requirements and confirmed one that meets the requirement.
While preparing the poster, I chose colors by taste and did not compare palettes to contrast requirements or confirm them.
As I edit the report, I benchmarked candidate cases to the theory’s conditions and verified the case that matches them.
As I edit the report, I inserted a case and did not benchmark it to the conditions or verify that it matches them.
Though I’m tired, I checked outstanding flags in my notes and confirmed the one that blocks tomorrow’s work.
Though I’m tired, I closed my notes and did not check flags or confirm which item blocks tomorrow’s work.
At the seminar, I drafted two questions, compared them to the central assumption, and verified which one to ask.
At the seminar, I asked the first question that occurred and did not compare it to the assumption or verify selection.
Once I saw the time limit, I ranked slides by necessity and confirmed which section to remove to fit the limit.
Once I saw the time limit, I deleted slides by length and did not rank necessity or confirm which section to remove.
During the final edit, I compared candidate charts for signal and steps, then verified the replacement to keep.
During the final edit, I kept the first chart and did not compare options for signal or verify the replacement.
On my last draft check, I scanned for required details, reviewed non-essentials, and confirmed which items to remove.
On my last draft check, I kept every detail and did not scan for required items, review extras, or confirm removals.
